text: moves the mad scavenger Tchitcherine
He has marched here
in his exile
his return
someone would come to sit in his seat
he had slipped into Trotsky’s
stepped outside only to piss
He had come to give the tribesmen out here
Young and old Kirghiz came in from the plain,
Tchitcherine will usually mosey down to the red džurt there
he’ll come outside to find his morning skies full of sheet-lightning
Tchitcherine tracks mud off the street into the Center,
get away from Kuropatkin’s troops and over the border into China
100 fleeing Kirghiz
surrounded and killed the darker refugees
brought out here by the Likbez agents
She had to come out here to learn
to go back now, back to a city?
of his own exile
Out into the bones of the backlands ride Tchitcherine and his faithful Kirghiz companion Džaqyp Qulan
Tchitcherine goes up to Snake’s jingling picket on the hillside
They’re riding away from the railroad
